title: Formal email & complaint letters
examples: What is the difference between a formal and informal email?
How do I start a complaint letter politely?
What should I include when I complain about a product?

explain.say: Today we learn to write formal emails and complaint letters. These are for serious topics.

items: Keep your tone serious and respectful.

explain.say: The structure of a formal letter has clear parts. You need a greeting, the body, and a closing.
When making a request, you must be very clear. State exactly what you want the recipient to do next.
A concrete example is complaining about a late package. You must mention the tracking number and the date it was expected.
For a real-life example, imagine your school canteen serves bad food. You should write a formal email to the head teacher about it.
A common mistake is sounding angry in writing. Remember to use polite phrases even when you are upset.

faq.q: Do I need to use full sentences in a formal email?
faq.a: Yes, you should use complete, full sentences. You should avoid text speak like 'u' or 'r'.
asks: Is it okay to use slang?

faq.q: What is the best way to start a complaint letter?
faq.a: Start by stating the purpose of your writing clearly and politely. You can say, 'I am writing to complain about...'
asks: How do I introduce my complaint?
What phrase should I use first?

faq.q: Should I include my contact details in the letter?
faq.a: Yes, always include your full name and contact details. This helps the person respond to you.
asks: Do I need to put my phone number?
Where should I put my address?

faq.q: If I am complaining about a product, what details must I include?
faq.a: You must include the product name, the model number, and the date you purchased it. These details are very important.
asks: Do I need a receipt number?

faq.q: Is it better to complain by email or by letter?
faq.a: Both are acceptable, but an email is often faster for quick responses. A formal printed letter can feel more serious.
asks: Which is faster, email or post?
When should I use a physical letter?

facts: A formal email requires a clear subject line.
The tone must remain polite, even when expressing dissatisfaction.
Always include specific dates and reference numbers in complaints.
A formal closing should match the level of formality used in the greeting.

quiz.say: If you are writing to a company about a broken toaster, what is the most appropriate opening phrase?
quiz.show: A) Hey guys, my toaster broke.

options.show: D) My toaster is broken, fix it.
options.say: D) My toaster is broken, fix it.

options.show: B) I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with...
options.say: B) I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with...

options.show: A) Hey guys, my toaster broke.
options.say: A) Hey guys, my toaster broke.

options.show: C) You need to fix this toaster right away.
options.say: C) You need to fix this toaster right away.

quiz.why: This option is polite and immediately sets a formal tone for the complaint.

wrong.0: This is too blunt and aggressive for professional writing.
wrong.2: This uses slang and is too informal for a complaint.
wrong.3: This is too demanding and lacks the polite register required.

quiz.say: You bought a book that arrived damaged. Which detail is most crucial to include in your complaint?
quiz.show: Date purchased, item name, and damage description

options.show: All three details are necessary for the recipient to help you.
options.say: All three details are necessary for the recipient to help you.

quiz.why: Including all these facts helps the company locate your purchase and understand the issue.

wrong.1: Without the date or damage, they cannot verify the claim.
wrong.2: Knowing the date alone does not tell them what is wrong with the item.
wrong.3: They need to know what item the damage belongs to.

quiz.say: When making a request in a formal complaint, what is the best approach?

options.show: Just stating the problem without asking for anything.
options.say: Just stating the problem without asking for anything.

options.show: Using vague language like 'sort it out'.
options.say: Using vague language like 'sort it out'.

options.show: Suggesting a clear, actionable solution politely.
options.say: Suggesting a clear, actionable solution politely.

quiz.why: Suggesting a solution shows you have thought through the problem and are looking for a resolution.

wrong.0: This is too aggressive and might make the recipient defensive.
wrong.1: The letter becomes useless if it does not state what action is required.
wrong.2: Vague requests make it impossible for the recipient to know what to do.
